answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear identity bond. To register, each agent locks a scarce-token bond, and the k-th identity funded from one source costs k squared times the base bond B. Picture a data farm on a karst plateau whose operator wants a grove of 1,000 sybil agents to sway votes, while an honest single node, juniper, pays only B. That grove owes the sum of k-squared times B for k=1 to 1000, about 334 million B, not 1,000 B. The superlinear curve makes mass fake identities economically impossible.
